The '''ATP Masters 1000''' tournaments, also known as Masters 1000 or ATP 1000 events, are an annual series of nine tennis tournaments featuring the top-ranked players on the [[ATP Tour]] since its inception in 1990.<ref>{{Cite web |date=Jun 27, 2018 |title=It's time for a grass-court Masters tournament |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/it-s-time-for-a-grass-court-masters-tournament |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231004150429/https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/it-s-time-for-a-grass-court-masters-tournament |archive-date=October 4, 2023 |access-date=10 September 2023 |publisher=Tennis.com}}</ref> The ATP 1000 events sit below the [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Tournaments|Grand Slam]] tournaments and the [[ATP Finals|year-end championships]] in prestige on the annual ATP Tour calendar; these tournaments plus the quadrennial [[Tennis at the Summer Olympics|Summer Olympics]] are collectively known as the '[[List of ATP Big Titles singles champions|Big Titles]]'.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Macpherson |first1=Paul |date=10 May 2016 |title=Big Titles: Federer Leads But Novak's Strike Rate Dazzles |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/federer-big-titles-2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210615150328/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/federer-big-titles-2016 |archive-date=June 15, 2021 |access-date=8 May 2021 |publisher=[[Association of Tennis Professionals|ATP]]}}</ref>

In singles, [[Novak Djokovic]] holds the record for the [[ATP Masters 1000 singles records and statistics#Title leaders|most ATP 1000 singles titles]] with 40.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ATP Masters 1000: Tournaments, Records, Stats |url=http://www.atptour.com/en/news/atp-masters-1000-stats-records-tournaments |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200726112419/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/atp-masters-1000-stats-records-tournaments |archive-date=July 26, 2020 |access-date=July 25, 2020 |website=ATP Tour}}</ref> By completing the career set of all nine current ATP 1000 series singles titles in [[2018 Western & Southern Open – Men's singles|2018]], Djokovic became the first player to achieve the [[ATP Masters 1000 singles records and statistics#Career Golden Masters|Career Golden Masters]] in singles.<ref name="GM">{{Cite web |date=19 August 2018 |title=Nine To Shine: Djokovic Claims Historic Cincy Crown |url=http://www.atptour.com/en/news/cincinnati-2018-final-federer-djokovic |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220309181131/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/cincinnati-2018-final-federer-djokovic |archive-date=9 March 2022 |website=ATP Tour}}</ref> In 2026, [[Jannik Sinner]] became the second, and youngest, player to complete the Career Golden Masters at the age of 24.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 May 2026 |title=Jannik Sinner wins Rome, becomes youngest player ever to complete Career Golden Masters |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/jannik-sinner-wins-rome-title-youngest-player-to-complete-career-golden-masters |access-date=19 May 2026 |publisher=Tennis.com}}</ref>

In doubles, the [[Bryan brothers]] ([[Bob Bryan|Bob]] and [[Mike Bryan|Mike]]) won a record [[ATP Masters 1000 doubles records and statistics|39 doubles titles]] as a team. [[Daniel Nestor]] and the Bryan brothers are the only doubles players to achieve the [[ATP Masters 1000 doubles records and statistics#Career Golden Masters|Career Golden Masters]].<ref name="Masters Sweep">{{Cite news |author=Patrick Johnston |date=2014-10-12 |title=Bryans achieve another record with Masters slam |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-men-shanghai-bryans-idUSKCN0I10BK20141012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211009175740/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-men-shanghai-bryans-idUSKCN0I10BK20141012 |archive-date=9 October 2021 |access-date=2021-09-15 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref> All three doubles players also won titles at 10 different tournaments. 

Out of the five male players who achieved the '''Career Golden Masters''', Daniel Nestor is the first player to achieve the feat in 2011<ref>{{Cite web |title=Daniel Nestor {{!}} Bio {{!}} ATP Tour {{!}} Tennis |url=http://www.atptour.com/en/players/daniel-nestor/n210/bio |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=ATP Tour |language=en}}</ref> and Sinner is the fastest player to complete the same feat in a record span of 33 months.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Novak Djokovic, Jannik Sinner & Career Golden Masters history {{!}} ATP Tour {{!}} Tennis |url=http://www.atptour.com/en/news/sinner-djokovic-career-golden-masters-rome-2026 |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=ATP Tour |language=en}}</ref> In [[2020 Western & Southern Open – Men's singles|2020]], Djokovic has become the only player to complete the Career Golden Masters twice.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 August 2020 |title=Novak Djokovic's Golden Rule: A Grandmaster Twice Over! {{!}} ATP Tour {{!}} Tennis |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/djokovic-raonic-ws-open-2020-final |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220309181302/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/djokovic-raonic-ws-open-2020-final |archive-date=9 March 2022 |website=ATP Tour}}</ref>
{{TOC limit|3}}

== History ==
The ATP Championship Series (Single Week) was introduced in 1990 with the inception of the ATP Tour by bringing together the nine most prestigious tournaments of the [[Grand Prix Super Series]] of the preceding [[ITF Grand Prix Circuit]]. Results in ATP 1000 events earn players more ranking points than regular tournaments but less than Grand Slam events or the year-end ATP Finals.

Up until 2007, most ATP Masters 1000 finals were contested as best-of-five-set matches, but from 2008 all events were decided in best-of-three-set matches.
As part of a shake-up of the tennis circuit in 2009, the Masters Series became the ATP Masters 1000,<ref>{{cite web |title=FAQ about PIF ATP Rankings |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/rankings/rankings-faq |access-date=6 May 2025 |website=ATP Tour |language=en}}</ref> with the addition of the number 1000 referring to the number of ranking points earned by the winner of each tournament. Contrary to earlier plans, the number of tournaments was not reduced from nine to eight and the [[Monte-Carlo Masters]] remained part of the series although, unlike the other events, it does not have a mandatory player commitment. The [[Hamburg European Open|Hamburg Masters]] event was downgraded to an [[ATP Tour 500]] event. The [[Madrid Open (tennis)|Madrid Open]] moved to May and onto clay courts. A new tournament in [[Shanghai Masters (tennis)|Shanghai]] replaced the Hamburg Masters and took over Madrid's former October indoor slot.

In 2011, six of the nine 1000 level tournaments were combined ATP and [[Women's Tennis Association|WTA]] events. In 2025, all tournaments introduced the [[Instant replay|Video Review]] system, starting with the [[2025 BNP Paribas Open|Indian Wells Open]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ATP announced introduction of Video Review across all ATP Masters 1000s |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/video-review-atp-masters-1000-2025 |website=atptour.com |access-date=10 February 2026 |date=6 February 2025}}</ref>

=== Series name ===
* 1990–1995: ATP Championship Series, Single Week
* 1996–1999: ATP Super 9
* 2000–2003: Tennis Masters Series
* 2004–2008: ATP Masters Series
* 2009–2018: ATP World Tour Masters 1000
* 2019–present: ATP Masters 1000

== Tournaments ==
Currently, the following nine tournaments are part of the ATP Masters 1000: [[Canadian Open (tennis)|Canadian Open]] (alternating yearly between [[Montreal]] and [[Toronto]]), [[Italian Open (tennis)|Italian Open]] (held in [[Rome]]), [[Indian Wells Open]], [[Miami Open (tennis)|Miami Open]], [[Monte-Carlo Masters]], [[Madrid Open (tennis)|Madrid Open]], [[Cincinnati Open]], [[Shanghai Masters (tennis)|Shanghai Masters]] and [[Paris Masters]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ATP Tour calendar |url=http://www.atptour.com/en/tournaments |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200725063122/https://www.atptour.com/en/tournaments |archive-date=July 25, 2020 |access-date=July 25, 2020 |website=ATPTour.com}}</ref> Since [[2009 ATP World Tour|2009]], five of the tournaments have been held on outdoor hard courts, three on clay and one on indoor hard court, whereas from [[1990 ATP Tour|1990]] until [[2008 ATP Tour|2008]] there were two indoor tournaments at the top-9 level.
In 2009, the [[Shanghai Masters (tennis)|Shanghai Masters]] replaced the [[Madrid Open (tennis)|Madrid Open]], which was until then held as an indoor event, in the eighth slot of the year with the Madrid Open switched to clay courts, replacing the [[Hamburg Open]] in the spring clay court season. The Shanghai Masters was designated as an outdoor event despite the facility having a retractable roof and having been used as the indoor venue for the ATP Finals from 2005 until 2008. Other than Hamburg, the tournaments defunct between 1990 and 2009 were Stockholm (1990–1994) and Stuttgart (1995–2001), which were held as indoor events in the eighth slot.

On October 23, 2025, the ATP announced that a new Masters 1000 tournament (the tenth on the calendar) will be held in [[Saudi Arabia]], likely beginning in 2028, although the specific date remains to be determined. The placement of the event on the ATP calendar has also not been announced. The field will be 56 players and the event will be non-mandatory. This will be the first time the ATP Masters 1000 events number ten in one calendar year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tennis.com |date=23 October 2025 |title=Saudi Arabia to host newly created 10th ATP Masters 1000 as early as 2028 |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/saudi-arabia-atp-masters-1000-2028 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260207210437/https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/saudi-arabia-atp-masters-1000-2028 |archive-date=7 February 2026 |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=Tennis.com |language=en}}</ref>
